findings.evidence: Commit subject: imperative verb plus what changed ("Add token refresh on 401"); the reason goes in the body. / README section: what it is, how to run it, then details.
findings.fix: Remove the commit-subject and README-order bullets because the model already follows these conventions. Keep only the error-message and help-text orderings, which correct real failure modes (apology and preamble).

findings.evidence: Restructure: active voice when the source names the actor, positive form, related words together, the key point at the end of the sentence.
findings.fix: Shorten this to the non-obvious qualifier, "active voice only when the source names the actor", because the generic Strunk rules are already in the elements-of-style reference.

findings.evidence: Edit branch steps 1-5 work at the level of a passage or sentence; no order is given for a multi-section document
findings.fix: Add one line for long documents: first cut or merge sections that repeat each other, then fix paragraph order, then do the sentence-level pass. Rewording sentences in a section that will be deleted wastes the edit.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list covers wording invariants but has no gotcha about document markup
findings.fix: Add a NEVER item: never drop or reflow Markdown structure (link targets, heading levels, list markers, front matter, table columns) while tightening, because a changed anchor or heading breaks inbound links and generated tables of contents.

findings.evidence: There is no eval for the "Tighten this with no text supplied" branch or for the Flag branch on fiction or quotations. tighten-prose has the vague assertion "Removes promotional phrases".
findings.fix: Add a no-text eval ("can you tighten this up?" with no text attached), with the assertion that it asks for the text and does not invent a sample. Add a quotation or fiction Flag eval. Make tighten-prose's first assertion name the phrases that must be removed, for example "groundbreaking", "cutting-edge" and "seamless".

findings.evidence: | Text whose voice must stay: the user says "keep our tone" or "brand voice" ... | Flag | numbered suggestions only; the original stays untouched |
findings.fix: Limit the Flag row to supplied text, and add a rule that a request to write new copy in a brand voice goes to Draft and copies the voice from the user's samples. As written, "write a tooltip in our brand voice" matches Flag, which has no original to suggest edits to.
